facts.claim: sales and use tax rate on adult-use cannabis
facts.source_name: Comptroller of Maryland, quarterly adult-use cannabis tax revenue reports
facts.verify: Rate rose from 9 to 12 percent on 2025-07-01 under the Budget Reconciliation and Financing Act of 2025. The Comptroller's quarterly releases describe Jul-Sep 2025 as the first full quarter at 12 percent.
facts.note: TRAP: the Comptroller's static page at marylandcomptroller.gov/cannabis.html still states 9 percent and is out of date. Cite the quarterly report, never that page. Re-verify before every Maryland publish, since a further increase to 15 percent was proposed for fiscal 2027 in the BRFA and may or may not have taken effect.

facts.claim: adult-use cannabis sales and use tax collected, January to March 2026
facts.verify: Headline figure 26.2 million for the January to March 2026 quarter

facts.claim: adult-use cannabis sales began in Maryland
facts.source_name: Comptroller of Maryland, adult-use cannabis tax page
facts.verify: Page states the cannabis sales and use tax took effect 2023-07-01, which is the start of legal adult-use sales
facts.note: Only the effective-date element of this page is used. Its 9 percent rate figure is stale, see md-sales-tax.

gaps: Licensed dispensary count: the MCA dispensary page cites 101 licensed entities but is marked archived and carries no as-of date. Pull the current count from the MCA 2026 data dashboard download before publishing any dispensary number.
License classes: MD distinguishes standard, micro, and incubator-space dispensary licenses plus social-equity rounds. Break the count down by class rather than publishing one aggregate.
Per-city counts for Baltimore, Silver Spring, Frederick, Annapolis: needed for city pages.
Zoning versus opt-out: MD localities zone rather than ban outright. Confirm the precise mechanism before writing the local-control sentence, since the CA framing does not transfer.
